item.title: Re: Scrutiny of the assisted dying bill is vital but obstruction in the House of Lords could mean it never becomes law
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, Scrutiny of assisted dying legislation aligns with a doctor's professional duty. It is not obstruction. The recent BMJ opinion piece by Ladies Hayter, Gerada and Rafferty suggests that thorough scrutiny of the assisted dying bill risks “obstruction.”¹ For doctors, this mindset raises red flags that our professional duties to patients are being sidelined. item.title: When GDP runs faster than demography: performance metrics cannot outrun population reality
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, Record-high stock indices and gross domestic product (GDP) figures are often cited as evidence of effective governance. Yet in many ageing societies, these numbers increasingly fail to translate into a sense of security among citizens. This disconnect is not merely perceptual; it reflects a structural mismatch between headline economic indicators and underlying demographic realities. Taiwan offers a revealing example. item.title: Re: Machine learning based screening of potential paper mill publications in cancer research: methodological and cross sectional study
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, Scancar and colleagues highlight the critical issue of paper mills in cancer research using machine learning[1]. However, several fundamental methodological limitations undermine the validity of their conclusions and raise serious concern regarding the model’s editorial applicability. item.title: Ignore the experts
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor An expert, we’re told, is someone with 10,000 hours under their belt. item.title: Re: Scarlett McNally: Shared decision making requires striking the right balance

item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor Lei’s editorial on reduced disease detection during the covid-19 pandemic rightly draws attention to how disruptions in routine care delayed diagnosis and exposed vulnerabilities in health systems (1). item.title: Screening for primary aldosteronism before potassium-sparing diuretics in resistant hypertension or hypokalaemia
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, Anisman and colleagues highlight potassium sparing diuretics as an effective option for resistant hypertension.[1] However, the prevalence of primary aldosteronism (PA) in patients with resistant hypertension ranges from 11.3% to 29.1%.[2] Despite this, PA remains undertested and therefore underdiagnosed.
